alt_text: Three-generation pedigree for Syndrome X. Squares represent males, circles females, and filled symbols affected individuals.
long_description: Generation I: I-1 is an affected female and I-2 an unaffected male; they are connected to the six Generation II individuals. II-1 is an affected male, II-2 an unaffected female, II-3 an affected female, II-4 an unaffected male, II-5 an unaffected male, and II-6 an unaffected female. II-3 and II-4 are connected as a couple, with four Generation III children: III-1 unaffected male, III-2 affected female, III-3 unaffected male, III-4 unaffected female. The legend explains sex and affected status. The question text separately states that II-4 is a known carrier; carrier status is not shaded in this diagram.

alt_text: Light-dependent photosynthesis schematic across a thylakoid membrane. Photosystem II, an electron transport chain, photosystem I and ATP synthase are shown. Lumen and stroma are labeled.
long_description: The thylakoid membrane is a vertical band, with lumen on the left and stroma on the right. Light reaches photosystem II and photosystem I. Electron arrows connect photosystem II to the electron transport chain, then to photosystem I and onward to NADP plus on the stroma side, where NADPH is formed. A proton arrow at the electron transport chain runs from stroma to lumen. A proton arrow through ATP synthase runs from lumen to stroma. ADP plus inorganic phosphate and ATP are shown on the stroma side. The diagram is schematic and does not specify molecule counts.
